Investigation into why the HPCSA fails to register foreign doctors

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Landmark case brought by a foreign qualified doctor against the HPCSA for failure to register highly skilled foreign doctors

Summary:
Obstetrician Mark Stevens fought for 5 years to get registered by the HPCSA. He took the HPCSA to court in March and is waiting to hear Judge Thlapi's verdict. If he wins it should set a precedent for other foreign doctors in a similar predicament. But its too late for Dr Uli Van der Merwe, SA citizen but qualified in German, Italy and USA. After two years of struggling to register she is leaving the country to work in Germany. The failure to register foreign doctors has been going on for so long that finally Minister of Health Dr Aaron Motsoaledi has ordered an independent investigation into what’s happening. UCT’s head of Medicine Prof Bongani Mayosi, and former chair of the committee who registers foreign doctors is heading up that investigation. Doctors say its a combination of complete administrative ineptitude, contradictory information, and a total lack of communication with applicants and when you do find somebody senior to fight your case they say its just too over worked.
The insert has 3 strong case studies.


Further information:
Dr Uli Van Der Merwe, SA citizen who is a trauma surgeon, orthopaedic surgeon and sports medicine specialist who ran a hospital in Tanzania performing operations in two theaters has been unable to register in SA for the last two years. She trained overseas in Germany, Italy and USA. All her qualifications have been certified by an appointed American agency. She is now leaving South Africa to work in Germany because the longer she isn't operating the more likely she is to lose her qualifications as a surgeon. She applied to work in one of the top hospitals in Germany and was accepted overnight. I will film her family packing the container to leave.

Dr Florian Von Groote, specialist Pulmologist, SA resident, has a job offer from Tygerburg hospital but hasn't been able to get registered for the last year. His description is that it’s a nightmare, they keep asking for different information, loose his papers, and forced him to write a general medicine exam after telling him it was a language and ethics exam. He last studied general medicine when he qualified as a doctor and has been a specialist Pulmologist for the last 6 years. The HPCSA refused to give him his results or let him see his paper, they will only tell him he has failed.

Dr Mark Stevens gynaecologist and obstetrician, married to a South African, has a SA residents permit but has been unable to register for the last 5 years. Finally he took the HPCSA to court. His case was heard in March 2015 by Judge Thlapi and he is waiting for the judgement. If she rules in his favour it will set a president for other foreign doctors.
All 3 doctors are happy to speak on camera.

Press Release:


Failing Foreign Doctors
South Africa has a critical shortage of doctors and specialists. So why are highly skilled foreign doctors desperate to make a difference in the country, being turned away? Carte Blanche investigates the ineffective Health Professions Council policies and administrative delays resulting in a devastating loss of medical expertise.


Script:


Script: Uli Van Der Merwe is packing up her family and returning to Germany. She was born in South Africa and is married to a South African. Uli studied in Germany, Italy and at Harvard to become a specialist Trauma and Orthopaedic surgeon. For the last two years she has been trying in vain to get registered by the Health Professions Council
Uli ” Tuesday evening I sent a letter to one of the two biggest and best hospitals in Germany and applied. Wednesday morning 5 past 8 they called me and said when can you start, and as happy as it made me …I am so angry that I cannot work here. The Western World takes me like that, and Africa says we don’t need you
Script: Uli was running a sizeable hospital in Tanzania when her parent’s in-law died, and her husband had to return to South Africa. Uli immediately applied to get registered
Uli Van der Merwe “Honestly it took me 5 months to eventually get somebody who had an idea what I have to do. I got every time different forms every time different answers nobody ever told me I had to first be verified in America.
Script: It took 6 months for her papers to be verified, and when the HPCSA confirmed they had received them, she thought the process would be a straight forward
Uli “ I have tried everything everything everything everything”
Devi ”Do you considered yourself South African?”
Uli Van der Merwe “Yes, I have always been more African that European always. I want to be definitely in Africa. Because you can really do something here
Links “There is an international shortage of doctors and nurses and every year more and more medical practioners are leaving SA, but foreign doctors that are desperate to work in South Africa are telling us that it is extremely difficult to get registered to work here
Script: German doctor Florian Von Groote is a specialist in internal medicine and Pulmonology focusing on the treatment of drug resistant TB and the diagnosis of lung cancer. He was registered for 5 years by the HPCSA while he was studying at Tygerberg hospital as part of his Pulmonology specialization, but completed it in Germany. When he applied to register in South Africa he hit a brick wall.
Florian “I don’t phone the HPCSA because I now I don’t get anywhere, its highly frustrating that I have to pay a lawyer to be assisted in a process that should happen automatically. The Germans have recognised every minute of my training in South Africa without any question, all I am asking is please recognise my German specialist exam,
Script: The HPCSA appears to disregard foreign doctor’s years of experience and specializations. They all have to write a general medicine exam. It’s like being asked to write matric again. Initially he was told it was a language and ethics which he was happy to write. But it turned out to be general medicine, which he hadn’t studied and not surprisingly he failed.
Florian “You get a generic answer every foreign practioner has to write the board exam it’s like a tape that keeps on playing”
Script: The HPCSA has 12 different professional boards, the largest being the medical and dental board which has several different sub- committees. Prof Gerhard Lindeque Deputy Dean at the School of Medicine in Pretoria is chair of the examination subcommittee which amongst other things looks at foreign doctor registrations
Devi” we are asking him to write a board exam as though he was some kind of junior
Lindeque ”Amazing.
Devi ”How would you feel if somebody asked you to do that?
Lindeque “Stunned.
Devi “So you agree this is a mess with Florian.”
Prof Lindeque “The committee never wanted this to happen.
Devi” But then how did it happen?
Lindeque “Because the HPCSA admin staff do things in their way.
Devi” But they are not sitting on the committee
Lindeque “Correct. I am stunned with you
Devi” But what gives them the right to do that?
Lindeque “It is a very good question.
Devi “Have you raised this.
Lindeque” Numerous times at all levels .
Devi “For Florian.
Lindeque” Indeed.
Devi “And?
Lindeque” To no avail
Script: The problems at the HPCSA are on the administrative side; they are supposed to implement the decisions made by the committees
Lindeque “There are also blockage that occur where members of the HPCSA staff actually wipe out the decisions of the committee.”
Devi “What do they do?
Lindeque “Well people will get a letter to say your case was heard at PTM at this and this date and you have been approved for example independent practice and then there is a PS at the bottom now these days that this whole thing has essentially been blocked by HPCSA because it is under a new revision”
Script: We told Prof Lindeque about Uli’s case, but as her application hadn’t come before the board, he had never heard of her
Prof Lindeque” If the person is not on the agenda we don’t know the person is there. I agree, as you said it’s sad I agree it sad. “
Script: Mark Heywood Director of human rights organization Section 27, says the situation at the HPCSA has worsened in the last year, and these delays are exacerbating the acute shortage of doctors in South Africa
Mark Heywood “By some peoples calculations that is costing us potentially 200 qualified doctors who would like to work in SA per annum who are being kept out just by bureaucracy and red tape”
Florian “Now after a year that I am still not registered I have told my attorney in Pretoria to prepare papers to go to court
Script: This is exactly what specialist obstetrician and gynaecologist Dr Mark Stevens did in March this year, after 5 years of trying to get registered he took the HPCSA to court and is waiting for the judgement. He thought his registration would be simple. He’s married to a South African, has permanent residents’ status and his degree from the Royal College in London, is recognised by the Health Professions Act.
Devi “Why are you speaking to us now because the last time we met we had to hide you identity
Mark “I asked to hide on legal advice and I was unsure how the legal process was going to unravel now the court has been heard and it’s in the public knowledge and I want to put this on camera and help other people in this situation”
Devi “So what was their main argument in court
Mark Stevens “Their main and only argument is that all foreign qualifications are not recognised so they have the right to evaluate every foreign qualification which flies in the face of the parliamentary act which has created a fast track of if you hold a certain qualification the Minister of Health has deemed it acceptable, the law is written in a very positive way to entice doctors into South Africa whereas the Health Council seem to be pushing them away “
Script: The problem was that Mark applied to register for Private Practice, allowed in the Health Professions Act for recognised specialist qualifications but Prof Lindeque says the HPCSA sees it differently
Lindeque “We were told that the fact that a person gets permanent residence doesn’t change it nor if he marries a South African doesn’t change the basic principle of 3 years in the public service. The regulation is intended to strengthen the public sector. There is no choice according to the current state of the regulations and my committee has to interpret the current state of the regulations “
Mark Heywood “Last year the Health Professions Council decided that it was going to categorise new incoming foreign doctors as community service doctors. Now a university community service doctor is somebody who has just got out of university and has been placed in a district hospital. A foreign doctor can have 20 or 30 years’ experience he or she can be a heart surgeon or a immune disease expert , they come to SA now they are classified as a community service doctor. And that was somebody in the HPCSA who wrote some legal opinion that said this is how we should interpret this act and then bang suddenly the whole system changes”
Links “If you want to practice as a doctor in SA you have to be registered with the HPCSA and pay your annual subscription yet members have very little say in how the organization is run”
Lindeque ‘The practioners in the country are canned lions they have to pay and they can’t really impact on any policy or proceedings.
Devi “ Are your hands tied ?”
Lindeque “Absolutely we make proposals about all these things. It is very hard to be in a committee where you have to follow a set of rules.
Links “This situation has been going on for years but the HPCSA refused to talk to us pending the outcome of an investigation recently ordered by the minister of health
Lindeque. “The investigation that the minister ordered a month ago was to look at efficiency, efficacy and the speed at which processes are taking place. The organization is run by the CEO and COO and they have to carry the full responsibility
Mark Heywood “I think our country is plagued by task teams and commissions and investigations to tell us what we already know . One of the problems of our country is that quite often it’s this person being connected to that person so you can’t quickly move against this person in the HPCSA because of these connections and so you have to look objective investigative process in order to justify eventually dealing with them and in the meantime the rot continues
Florian “I am a permanent resident in this country I have got a specialist degree from a foreign country, I have got a job offer for a part time position at a government hospital, but still I can’t work as a doctor
Mark Stevens “It’s absolutely sole destroying I have got so much to give, people have been offering me jobs been desperate for me to come
Uli” We had the hopes ok somehow it will work out, we thought ok you must see moss there is somebody who has the ability to do things and that can help and you say no, why?

And that was somebody in the HPCSA who wrote some legal opinion that said this is how we should interpret this act and then bang suddenly the whole system changes” Links “If you want to practice as a doctor in SA you have to be registered with the HPCSA and pay your annual subscription yet members have very little say in how the organization is run” Lindeque ‘The practioners in the country are canned lions they have to pay and they can’t really impact on any policy or proceedings. Devi “ Are your hands tied ?” Lindeque “Absolutely we make proposals about all these things. It is very hard to be in a committee where you have to follow a set of rules. Links “This situation has been going on for years but the HPCSA refused to talk to us pending the outcome of an investigation recently ordered by the minister of health Lindeque. “The investigation that the minister ordered a month ago was to look at efficiency, efficacy and the speed at which processes are taking place. The organization is run by the CEO and COO and they have to carry the full responsibility Mark Heywood “I think our country is plagued by task teams and commissions and investigations to tell us what we already know . One of the problems of our country is that quite often it’s this person being connected to that person so you can’t quickly move against this person in the HPCSA because of these connections and so you have to look objective investigative process in order to justify eventually dealing with them and in the meantime the rot continues Florian “I am a permanent resident in this country I have got a specialist degree from a foreign country, I have got a job offer for a part time position at a government hospital, but still I can’t work as a doctor Mark Stevens “It’s absolutely sole destroying I have got so much to give, people have been offering me jobs been desperate for me to come Uli” We had the hopes ok somehow it will work out, we thought ok you must see moss there is somebody who has the ability to do things and that can help and you say no, why? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Landmark case brought by a foreign qualified doctor against the HPCSA for failure to register highly skilled foreign doctors
metadata.Summary: Obstetrician Mark Stevens fought for 5 years to get registered by the HPCSA. He took the HPCSA to court in March and is waiting to hear Judge Thlapi's verdict. If he wins it should set a precedent for other foreign doctors in a similar predicament. But its too late for Dr Uli Van der Merwe, SA citizen but qualified in German, Italy and USA. After two years of struggling to register she is leaving the country to work in Germany. The failure to register foreign doctors has been going on for so long that finally Minister of Health Dr Aaron Motsoaledi has ordered an independent investigation into what’s happening. UCT’s head of Medicine Prof Bongani Mayosi, and former chair of the committee who registers foreign doctors is heading up that investigation. Doctors say its a combination of complete administrative ineptitude, contradictory information, and a total lack of communication with applicants and when you do find somebody senior to fight your case they say its just too over worked. The insert has 3 strong case studies.
metadata.Further information: Dr Uli Van Der Merwe, SA citizen who is a trauma surgeon, orthopaedic surgeon and sports medicine specialist who ran a hospital in Tanzania performing operations in two theaters has been unable to register in SA for the last two years. She trained overseas in Germany, Italy and USA. All her qualifications have been certified by an appointed American agency. She is now leaving South Africa to work in Germany because the longer she isn't operating the more likely she is to lose her qualifications as a surgeon. She applied to work in one of the top hospitals in Germany and was accepted overnight. I will film her family packing the container to leave. Dr Florian Von Groote, specialist Pulmologist, SA resident, has a job offer from Tygerburg hospital but hasn't been able to get registered for the last year. His description is that it’s a nightmare, they keep asking for different information, loose his papers, and forced him to write a general medicine exam after telling him it was a language and ethics exam. He last studied general medicine when he qualified as a doctor and has been a specialist Pulmologist for the last 6 years. The HPCSA refused to give him his results or let him see his paper, they will only tell him he has failed. Dr Mark Stevens gynaecologist and obstetrician, married to a South African, has a SA residents permit but has been unable to register for the last 5 years. Finally he took the HPCSA to court. His case was heard in March 2015 by Judge Thlapi and he is waiting for the judgement. If she rules in his favour it will set a president for other foreign doctors. All 3 doctors are happy to speak on camera.
